subject: physics_2

mark_split.label: The sign rule and the net current
The line integral round a circle

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: ∮B·dl = μ₀i over a closed path, with the enclosed currents signed by the right-hand rule for the chosen sense of travel; the book's figure gives i = i₁ − i₂ − i₃ + i₄ for its own choice of sense, which is reproduced here. The verification uses a circular path round a long straight wire, where B is constant in magnitude and along dl, giving B(2πr) = μ₀i. The book's printed question reads 'ampere's law'; capitalised here as a proper name, and the space before the question mark is dropped.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The sign rule is the line most students skip. Say which currents count positive and write the signed sum before you go near the integral.

steps.label: A closed path round four currents
steps.margin_note: One closed path with four currents through it: two into the page (⊗) and two out of it (⊙). B and the element dl are marked on the path.
steps.why: The law is about a path, not about a wire, so the picture has to show the path first and the currents second — the shape of the path never enters the answer.
common_mistakes: Drawing the currents outside the path. Only currents THROUGH the path are counted.
Drawing B along the radius. B is taken along the path at the element dl.

recall.must_convey: That a closed path is drawn with currents passing through it, some into the page and some out of it.
accept: currents into and out of the page
mark B and dl on the path
reject: B equals mu nought i by two pi r

steps.memory_tip: Draw the loop first, then drop the currents through it.

steps.label: The statement
lines: Ampere's law: the line integral of the
magnetic induction B round any closed path is
equal to μ₀ times the net current enclosed by
that path.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say 'round any closed path' and 'net current enclosed' — both phrases carry the mark.
steps.why: The word 'any' is the whole strength of the law: the same answer comes out for every path round the same current, so a path can be chosen to make the integral easy.
common_mistakes: Saying total current instead of enclosed current. A current outside the path adds nothing.
Writing μ₀ on the wrong side, as ∮B·dl / μ₀ = i without saying so.

recall.must_convey: That the line integral of B round a closed path equals μ₀ times the enclosed current.
accept: line integral of B dot dl
mu nought times the current enclosed
reject: i one minus i two minus i three plus i four

steps.memory_tip: Walk once round the loop adding B·dl; the total only counts what you walked around.

steps.label: The sign rule and the net current
lines: A closed path may enclose several currents.
Fix a sense of travel round the path. A
current whose direction follows the right
hand rule for that sense is taken as
positive, and a current in the opposite
direction as negative.
In the figure i₁ and i₄ go into the page (⊗)
and are positive, while i₂ and i₃ come out of
the page (⊙) and are negative.
Currents outside the path are not counted.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The signed sum, with one line saying why two of the four carry a minus sign.
steps.why: Signs matter because two equal currents in opposite directions through the same path give zero line integral — the fields they make cancel round the loop.
common_mistakes: Adding all four currents with plus signs.
Counting a current that lies outside the path.

recall.must_convey: That the enclosed currents are added with signs fixed by direction, giving i = i₁ − i₂ − i₃ + i₄ here.
accept: currents into the page positive out of the page negative
i one minus i two minus i three plus i four

steps.memory_tip: One way in is a plus, the other way is a minus; anything outside the loop is a zero.

steps.label: The line integral round a circle
lines: Take a long straight wire carrying a current
i, and choose the closed path to be a circle
of radius r with the wire through its centre.
By symmetry B has the same size at every
point of the circle and is along the tangent,
so B and dl point the same way and the angle
between them is 0°.

lines.text: ∮ B · dl = ∮ B dl cos 0° = B ∮ dl

steps.margin_note: Third mark. Symmetry lets B come out of the integral, and the remaining integral is just the circumference.
steps.why: B can be taken outside the integral only because the circle is chosen so that B has the same size everywhere on it; that choice is the whole method.
common_mistakes: Leaving B inside the integral. On this path B is constant, so it comes out.
Writing ∮dl = πr². The path length of a circle is 2πr, not its area.

recall.must_convey: That on a circle round the wire B is constant and along dl, so the integral becomes B times 2πr.
accept: circle of radius r round the wire
B is constant and along dl
reject: B equals mu nought i by two pi r

steps.memory_tip: Same B all round means B steps outside the integral and only the circumference is left.

steps.label: The result
lines: The magnetic induction of a long straight
wire at a distance r is
Putting this in the previous step,
The radius r cancels, so the result does not
depend on the size of the path.
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Show r cancelling — that cancellation is the point of the whole step.
steps.why: B falls off as 1/r while the path length grows as r, so the two changes cancel exactly; that is why the line integral depends only on the enclosed current.
common_mistakes: Leaving r in the final answer. It must cancel.
Writing 2π in the answer. The 2π cancels with the one in B.

recall.must_convey: That substituting B = μ₀i/2πr gives ∮B·dl = μ₀i, with r cancelling.
accept: mu nought i by two pi r into two pi r
line integral equals mu nought i
reject: B is constant on the circle

steps.memory_tip: Field down by r, path up by r: the two cancel and only μ₀i survives.
